1	"""In-process, deterministic in-memory actor runtime.
2	
3	The runtime is deliberately single-process and synchronous: callers register
4	named actors, deliver messages to their mailboxes and explicitly advance
5	processing with :meth:`ActorRuntime.run`. Scheduling is fully determined by
6	registration order, message priority and delivery id -- never by wall-clock
7	time, randomness or thread interleaving.
8	
9	Time is just another explicitly replayed input: a logical clock starts at 0
10	and only moves when the caller calls :meth:`ActorRuntime.advance`. Timed
11	deliveries are held outside the mailboxes until their deadline; at a deadline
12	that is also their expiry tick expiry wins, so such a message never reaches a
13	handler.
14	"""
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import copy
18	import heapq
19	from typing import Any, Callable, NamedTuple
20	
21	__all__ = [
22	    "ActorContext",
23	    "ActorDataCopyError",
24	    "ActorExecutionError",
25	    "ActorRuntime",
26	    "AdvanceResult",
27	    "TraceEntry",
28	]
29	
30	
31	class TraceEntry(NamedTuple):
32	    """One completed message processing, in completion order.
33	
34	    ``state_before`` and ``state_after`` are independent snapshots; mutating
35	    them never affects the runtime or later queries.
36	    """
37	
38	    message_id: int
39	    actor_name: str
40	    priority: int
41	    state_before: Any
42	    state_after: Any
43	
44	
45	class AdvanceResult(NamedTuple):
46	    """Outcome of one :meth:`ActorRuntime.advance` call.
47	
48	    ``time`` is the clock value after the advance. ``released`` and
49	    ``expired`` are the message ids of the deliveries that respectively
50	    entered a mailbox or were dropped. Both lists are stably ordered by the
51	    tick the event happened at and then by message id.
52	    """
53	
54	    time: int
55	    released: tuple[int, ...]
56	    expired: tuple[int, ...]
57	
58	
59	class ActorDataCopyError(Exception):
60	    """Raised when a message or state cannot be deep-copied.
61	
62	    :meth:`ActorRuntime.send` raises it directly when the message cannot be
63	    copied; :meth:`ActorRuntime.run` reports a copy failure during processing
64	    as an :class:`ActorExecutionError` whose ``original`` is an
65	    ``ActorDataCopyError``. Either way nothing is committed: no mailbox
66	    change, no state change, no derived delivery, no trace entry and no
67	    consumed message id. ``what`` names the data being copied and
68	    ``original`` is the exception the copy raised.
69	    """
70	
71	    def __init__(self, what: str, original: BaseException):
72	        self.what = what
73	        self.original = original
74	        super().__init__(
75	            f"failed to deep-copy {what}: "
76	            f"{type(original).__name__}: {original}"
77	        )
78	
79	
80	class ActorExecutionError(Exception):
81	    """Raised by :meth:`ActorRuntime.run` when a message handler fails.
82	
83	    The failing message stays unacknowledged in its actor's mailbox and no
84	    state or derived delivery is committed for it. Messages completed earlier
85	    in the same :meth:`~ActorRuntime.run` call remain committed.
86	    """
87	
88	    def __init__(self, actor_name: str, message_id: int, original: BaseException):
89	        self.actor_name = actor_name
90	        self.message_id = message_id
91	        self.original = original
92	        super().__init__(
93	            f"actor {actor_name!r} failed while handling message {message_id}: "
94	            f"{type(original).__name__}: {original}"
95	        )
96	
97	
98	class ActorContext:
99	    """Handle passed to message handlers for sending derived messages.
100	
101	    Messages sent through :meth:`send` are buffered and only enter the target
102	    mailboxes after the current handler returns successfully.
103	    """
104	
105	    def __init__(self, runtime: "ActorRuntime"):
106	        self._runtime = runtime
107	        self._pending: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []
108	
109	    def send(self, target: str, message: Any) -> None:
110	        """Buffer a message for a registered actor with default priority 0.
111	
112	        Raises :class:`LookupError` if ``target`` is not registered. Raising
113	        inside the handler aborts the current processing exactly like any
114	        other handler exception.
115	        """
116	        if target not in self._runtime._actors:
117	            raise LookupError(f"unknown actor: {target!r}")
118	        self._pending.append((target, message))
119	
120	
121	Handler = Callable[[Any, Any, ActorContext], Any]
122	
123	
124	def _copy_data(what: str, value: Any) -> Any:
125	    """Deep-copy ``value``, reporting any failure as ActorDataCopyError."""
126	    try:
127	        return copy.deepcopy(value)
128	    except Exception as exc:
129	        raise ActorDataCopyError(what, exc) from exc
130	
131	
132	class _Actor:
133	    __slots__ = ("name", "state", "handler", "mailbox", "order")
134	
135	    def __init__(self, name: str, state: Any, handler: Handler, order: int):
136	        self.name = name
137	        self.state = state
138	        self.handler = handler
139	        self.order = order
140	        # Heap of (-priority, message_id, message); message_id is unique, so
141	        # the message object never participates in comparison.
142	        self.mailbox: list[tuple[int, int, Any]] = []
143	
144	
145	class _ScheduledDelivery:
146	    """A timed delivery held outside the mailboxes until its deadline."""
147	
148	    __slots__ = (
149	        "message_id", "actor", "priority", "message",
150	        "scheduled_at", "release_at", "expire_at",
151	    )
152	
153	    def __init__(self, message_id: int, actor: _Actor, priority: int,
154	                 message: Any, scheduled_at: int, release_at: int,
155	                 expire_at: int | None):
156	        self.message_id = message_id
157	        self.actor = actor
158	        self.priority = priority
159	        self.message = message
160	        self.scheduled_at = scheduled_at
161	        self.release_at = release_at
162	        # None means the delivery never expires.
163	        self.expire_at = expire_at
164	
165	
166	class ActorRuntime:
167	    """Deterministic in-memory actor runtime."""
168	
169	    def __init__(self) -> None:
170	        self._actors: dict[str, _Actor] = {}
171	        self._trace: list[TraceEntry] = []
172	        self._next_message_id = 1
173	        self._clock = 0
174	        # Pending timed deliveries, kept in scheduling (message-id) order;
175	        # _release_due scans and rebuilds it.
176	        self._scheduled: list[_ScheduledDelivery] = []
177	
178	    # -- registration -----------------------------------------------------
179	
180	    def register(self, name: str, initial_state: Any, handler: Handler) -> None:
181	        """Register a named actor.
182	
183	        Raises :class:`ValueError` when ``name`` is empty or already
184	        registered; a failed registration changes nothing.
185	        """
186	        if not isinstance(name, str) or name == "":
187	            raise ValueError("actor name must be a non-empty string")
188	        if name in self._actors:
189	            raise ValueError(f"actor already registered: {name!r}")
190	        self._actors[name] = _Actor(
191	            name, copy.deepcopy(initial_state), handler, len(self._actors)
192	        )
193	
194	    # -- delivery ---------------------------------------------------------
195	
196	    def send(self, target: str, message: Any, priority: int = 0) -> int:
197	        """Deliver a message to ``target``'s mailbox and return its id.
198	
199	        Ids are monotonically increasing within the runtime. Higher
200	        ``priority`` is processed first; equal priority is processed in id
201	        order. Raises :class:`TypeError` if ``priority`` is not an integer,
202	        :class:`LookupError` if ``target`` is unknown and
203	        :class:`ActorDataCopyError` if ``message`` cannot be deep-copied;
204	        a failed delivery consumes no id and changes no mailbox.
205	        """
206	        if not isinstance(priority, int) or isinstance(priority, bool):
207	            raise TypeError("priority must be an integer")
208	        actor = self._actors.get(target)
209	        if actor is None:
210	            raise LookupError(f"unknown actor: {target!r}")
211	        # Copy before assigning an id: a failed copy leaves the mailbox,
212	        # the trace, the actor state and the next message id untouched.
213	        stored = _copy_data("message", message)
214	        message_id = self._next_message_id
215	        self._next_message_id += 1
216	        heapq.heappush(actor.mailbox, (-priority, message_id, stored))
217	        return message_id
218	
219	    def schedule(self, target: str, message: Any, delay: int,
220	                 ttl: int | None = None, priority: int = 0) -> int:
221	        """Schedule ``message`` for ``target`` at a future logical tick.
222	
223	        Returns the delivery's id, taken from the same runtime-wide monotonic
224	        sequence as :meth:`send`. ``delay`` is the number of ticks counted
225	        from the current clock: the message is released when the clock reaches
226	        ``now + delay``. A ``delay`` of 0 releases it immediately unless it is
227	        already expired. ``ttl`` is the number of ticks the delivery stays
228	        alive after scheduling; when the clock reaches ``scheduled_at + ttl``
229	        the delivery expires without ever entering a mailbox or reaching a
230	        handler. At a tick that is both deadline and expiry, expiry wins.
231	
232	        Raises :class:`TypeError` for wrong argument types, :class:`ValueError`
233	        for out-of-range ``delay``/``ttl``, :class:`LookupError` for an
234	        unknown ``target`` and :class:`ActorDataCopyError` if ``message``
235	        cannot be deep-copied; a failed schedule consumes no id and queues
236	        nothing.
237	        """
238	        if not isinstance(priority, int) or isinstance(priority, bool):
239	            raise TypeError("priority must be an integer")
240	        if not isinstance(delay, int) or isinstance(delay, bool):
241	            raise TypeError("delay must be an integer")
242	        if delay < 0:
243	            raise ValueError("delay must be a non-negative integer")
244	        if ttl is not None and (
245	            not isinstance(ttl, int) or isinstance(ttl, bool)
246	        ):
247	            raise TypeError("ttl must be None or an integer")
248	        if ttl is not None and ttl <= 0:
249	            raise ValueError("ttl must be a positive integer or None")
250	        actor = self._actors.get(target)
251	        if actor is None:
252	            raise LookupError(f"unknown actor: {target!r}")
253	        # Copy before assigning an id: a failed copy queues nothing and
254	        # consumes no id, exactly like send.
255	        stored = _copy_data("message", message)
256	        message_id = self._next_message_id
257	        self._next_message_id += 1
258	        scheduled_at = self._clock
259	        release_at = scheduled_at + delay
260	        expire_at = None if ttl is None else scheduled_at + ttl
261	        if delay == 0:
262	            # ttl is a strictly positive integer, so a zero-delay delivery is
263	            # never already expired: it enters the mailbox straight away.
264	            heapq.heappush(actor.mailbox, (-priority, message_id, stored))
265	        else:
266	            self._scheduled.append(
267	                _ScheduledDelivery(
268	                    message_id, actor, priority, stored,
269	                    scheduled_at, release_at, expire_at,
270	                )
271	            )
272	        return message_id
273	
274	    # -- logical clock ----------------------------------------------------
275	
276	    def clock(self) -> int:
277	        """Return the current logical tick (initially 0)."""
278	        return self._clock
279	
280	    def advance(self, ticks: int) -> AdvanceResult:
281	        """Move the clock forward ``ticks`` and settle due deliveries.
282	
283	        ``ticks`` must be a non-boolean positive integer; otherwise
284	        :class:`TypeError`/:class:`ValueError` is raised and nothing changes.
285	        The clock moves to the new tick first; then every pending delivery is
286	        settled: one whose deadline has been reached is released into its
287	        actor's mailbox with its scheduled id and priority, while one whose
288	        ttl has elapsed expires and is dropped. When both happen at the same
289	        tick expiry wins, so the message never reaches a handler. Released and
290	        expired ids are returned stably ordered by event tick and then by id.
291	        Releasing never invokes a handler and never writes a trace entry; use
292	        :meth:`run` afterwards to process the mail.
293	        """
294	        if not isinstance(ticks, int) or isinstance(ticks, bool):
295	            raise TypeError("ticks must be an integer")
296	        if ticks <= 0:
297	            raise ValueError("ticks must be a positive integer")
298	
299	        new_time = self._clock + ticks
300	        released: list[tuple[int, int]] = []  # (release_at, id)
301	        expired: list[tuple[int, int]] = []   # (expire_at, id)
302	        remaining: list[_ScheduledDelivery] = []
303	        # _scheduled stays in message-id (scheduling) order; the event lists
304	        # are sorted by event tick and id afterwards, so the scan order is
305	        # irrelevant to the stable result.
306	        for delivery in self._scheduled:
307	            if (
308	                delivery.expire_at is not None
309	                and delivery.expire_at <= new_time
310	                and delivery.expire_at <= delivery.release_at
311	            ):
312	                # The ttl elapsed no later than the deadline: expiry at
313	                # expire_at. Equality with the deadline is decided in favour
314	                # of expiry, so a same-tick message never reaches a handler.
315	                expired.append((delivery.expire_at, delivery.message_id))
316	                continue
317	            if new_time >= delivery.release_at:
318	                # The deadline was reached during this advance. Even if the
319	                # ttl elapses at a later tick inside the same jump, the
320	                # delivery was released at its deadline and is ordinary
321	                # mailbox mail from then on; the ttl only guards the wait.
322	                heapq.heappush(
323	                    delivery.actor.mailbox,
324	                    (-delivery.priority, delivery.message_id,
325	                     delivery.message),
326	                )
327	                released.append((delivery.release_at, delivery.message_id))
328	                continue
329	            remaining.append(delivery)
330	
331	        self._scheduled = remaining
332	        self._clock = new_time
333	        released.sort(key=lambda event: (event[0], event[1]))
334	        expired.sort(key=lambda event: (event[0], event[1]))
335	        return AdvanceResult(
336	            new_time,
337	            tuple(message_id for _, message_id in released),
338	            tuple(message_id for _, message_id in expired),
339	        )
340	
341	    # -- execution --------------------------------------------------------
342	    def run(self, limit: int | None = None) -> int:
343	        """Process pending messages until mailboxes empty or ``limit`` hit.
344	
345	        Derived messages become eligible only after the handling message
346	        completes. The first handler failure aborts the run: an ordinary
347	        exception is raised as :class:`ActorExecutionError`, while a
348	        :class:`BaseException` that is not an :class:`Exception` (such as
349	        :class:`KeyboardInterrupt`) propagates unchanged. A failure to
350	        deep-copy the state, the message, the handler result or a buffered
351	        derived message is raised as :class:`ActorExecutionError` whose
352	        ``original`` is an :class:`ActorDataCopyError`. Either way the
353	        failing message stays pending and nothing is committed for it.
354	        Returns the number of messages completed by this call.
355	        """
356	        if limit is not None and (
357	            not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool) or limit <= 0
358	        ):
359	            raise ValueError("limit must be a positive integer or None")
360	
361	        processed = 0
362	        while limit is None or processed < limit:
363	            actor = None
364	            for candidate in self._actors.values():  # registration order
365	                if candidate.mailbox:
366	                    actor = candidate
367	                    break
368	            if actor is None:
369	                break
370	
371	            neg_priority, message_id, message = heapq.heappop(actor.mailbox)
372	            priority = -neg_priority
373	            try:
374	                # Every copy the commit depends on is made up front, so a
375	                # copy failure (custom __deepcopy__, an exception raised
376	                # while copying) commits nothing: the message goes back to
377	                # the mailbox with its original priority and no state,
378	                # derived delivery, id or trace entry is produced.
379	                state_before = _copy_data(
380	                    "state before processing", actor.state
381	                )
382	
383	                # Hand the handler private copies so a failure (including an
384	                # in-place mutation before raising) can never commit state
385	                # or alter the message kept in the mailbox.
386	                context = ActorContext(self)
387	                try:
388	                    new_state = actor.handler(
389	                        _copy_data("actor state", actor.state),
390	                        _copy_data("message", message),
391	                        context,
392	                    )
393	                except BaseException as exc:
394	                    # Ordinary exceptions are wrapped; BaseException
395	                    # subclasses that are not Exception (KeyboardInterrupt,
396	                    # SystemExit, ...) propagate unchanged.
397	                    if isinstance(exc, Exception):
398	                        raise ActorExecutionError(
399	                            actor.name, message_id, exc
400	                        ) from exc
401	                    raise
402	
403	                # Stage the commit: the returned state and every buffered
404	                # derived message are copied before anything becomes
405	                # visible, so even a failure in the last derived copy hides
406	                # the earlier ones and consumes no id.
407	                committed_state = _copy_data("handler result", new_state)
408	                staged = [
409	                    (target, _copy_data("derived message", derived))
410	                    for target, derived in context._pending
411	                ]
412	                trace_state = _copy_data("handler result", committed_state)
413	            except ActorDataCopyError as exc:
414	                heapq.heappush(actor.mailbox, (neg_priority, message_id, message))
415	                raise ActorExecutionError(
416	                    actor.name, message_id, exc
417	                ) from exc
418	            except BaseException:
419	                # Keep the message unacknowledged; commit nothing. The
420	                # message stays pending either way.
421	                heapq.heappush(actor.mailbox, (neg_priority, message_id, message))
422	                raise
423	
424	            # Commit: only runtime-owned bookkeeping below, so nothing here
425	            # can fail because of user data. Derived sends enqueue only
426	            # after successful completion.
427	            for derived_target, stored in staged:
428	                derived_id = self._next_message_id
429	                self._next_message_id += 1
430	                derived_actor = self._actors[derived_target]
431	                heapq.heappush(derived_actor.mailbox, (0, derived_id, stored))
432	
433	            actor.state = committed_state
434	            self._trace.append(
435	                TraceEntry(
436	                    message_id=message_id,
437	                    actor_name=actor.name,
438	                    priority=priority,
439	                    state_before=state_before,
440	                    state_after=trace_state,
441	                )
442	            )
443	            processed += 1
444	
445	        return processed
446	
447	    # -- read-only queries ------------------------------------------------
448	
449	    def get_state(self, actor_name: str) -> Any:
450	        """Return an independent snapshot of the actor's current state."""
451	        actor = self._require_actor(actor_name)
452	        return copy.deepcopy(actor.state)
453	
454	    def pending_count(self, actor_name: str) -> int:
455	        """Return the number of unprocessed messages for the actor.
456	
457	        Only messages that have already entered the mailbox are counted;
458	        scheduled deliveries that have not been released (and not expired) are
459	        reported separately by :meth:`scheduled_count`.
460	        """
461	        actor = self._require_actor(actor_name)
462	        return len(actor.mailbox)
463	
464	    def scheduled_count(self, actor_name: str) -> int:
465	        """Return the actor's deliveries neither released nor expired.
466	
467	        Raises :class:`LookupError` for an unknown actor.
468	        """

"""In-process, deterministic in-memory actor runtime.

The runtime is deliberately single-process and synchronous: callers register
named actors, deliver messages to their mailboxes and explicitly advance
processing with :meth:`ActorRuntime.run`. Scheduling is fully determined by
registration order, message priority and delivery id -- never by wall-clock
time, randomness or thread interleaving.

Time is just another explicitly replayed input: a logical clock starts at 0
and only moves when the caller calls :meth:`ActorRuntime.advance`. Timed
deliveries are held outside the mailboxes until their deadline; at a deadline
that is also their expiry tick expiry wins, so such a message never reaches a
handler.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import heapq
from typing import Any, Callable, NamedTuple

__all__ = [
    "ActorContext",
    "ActorDataCopyError",
    "ActorExecutionError",
    "ActorRuntime",
    "AdvanceResult",
    "TraceEntry",
]


class TraceEntry(NamedTuple):
    """One completed message processing, in completion order.

    ``state_before`` and ``state_after`` are independent snapshots; mutating
    them never affects the runtime or later queries.
    """

    message_id: int
    actor_name: str
    priority: int
    state_before: Any
    state_after: Any


class AdvanceResult(NamedTuple):
    """Outcome of one :meth:`ActorRuntime.advance` call.

    ``time`` is the clock value after the advance. ``released`` and
    ``expired`` are the message ids of the deliveries that respectively
    entered a mailbox or were dropped. Both lists are stably ordered by the
    tick the event happened at and then by message id.
    """

    time: int
    released: tuple[int, ...]
    expired: tuple[int, ...]


class ActorDataCopyError(Exception):
    """Raised when a message or state cannot be deep-copied.

    :meth:`ActorRuntime.send` raises it directly when the message cannot be
    copied; :meth:`ActorRuntime.run` reports a copy failure during processing
    as an :class:`ActorExecutionError` whose ``original`` is an
    ``ActorDataCopyError``. Either way nothing is committed: no mailbox
    change, no state change, no derived delivery, no trace entry and no
    consumed message id. ``what`` names the data being copied and
    ``original`` is the exception the copy raised.
    """

    def __init__(self, what: str, original: BaseException):
        self.what = what
        self.original = original
        super().__init__(
            f"failed to deep-copy {what}: "
            f"{type(original).__name__}: {original}"
        )


class ActorExecutionError(Exception):
    """Raised by :meth:`ActorRuntime.run` when a message handler fails.

    The failing message stays unacknowledged in its actor's mailbox and no
    state or derived delivery is committed for it. Messages completed earlier
    in the same :meth:`~ActorRuntime.run` call remain committed.
    """

    def __init__(self, actor_name: str, message_id: int, original: BaseException):
        self.actor_name = actor_name
        self.message_id = message_id
        self.original = original
        super().__init__(
            f"actor {actor_name!r} failed while handling message {message_id}: "
            f"{type(original).__name__}: {original}"
        )


class ActorContext:
    """Handle passed to message handlers for sending derived messages.

    Messages sent through :meth:`send` are buffered and only enter the target
    mailboxes after the current handler returns successfully.
    """

    def __init__(self, runtime: "ActorRuntime"):
        self._runtime = runtime
        self._pending: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []

    def send(self, target: str, message: Any) -> None:
        """Buffer a message for a registered actor with default priority 0.

        Raises :class:`LookupError` if ``target`` is not registered. Raising
        inside the handler aborts the current processing exactly like any
        other handler exception.
        """
        if target not in self._runtime._actors:
            raise LookupError(f"unknown actor: {target!r}")
        self._pending.append((target, message))


Handler = Callable[[Any, Any, ActorContext], Any]


def _copy_data(what: str, value: Any) -> Any:
    """Deep-copy ``value``, reporting any failure as ActorDataCopyError."""
    try:
        return copy.deepcopy(value)
    except Exception as exc:
        raise ActorDataCopyError(what, exc) from exc


class _Actor:
    __slots__ = ("name", "state", "handler", "mailbox", "order")

    def __init__(self, name: str, state: Any, handler: Handler, order: int):
        self.name = name
        self.state = state
        self.handler = handler
        self.order = order
        # Heap of (-priority, message_id, message); message_id is unique, so
        # the message object never participates in comparison.
        self.mailbox: list[tuple[int, int, Any]] = []


class _ScheduledDelivery:
    """A timed delivery held outside the mailboxes until its deadline."""

    __slots__ = (
        "message_id", "actor", "priority", "message",
        "scheduled_at", "release_at", "expire_at",
    )

    def __init__(self, message_id: int, actor: _Actor, priority: int,
                 message: Any, scheduled_at: int, release_at: int,
                 expire_at: int | None):
        self.message_id = message_id
        self.actor = actor
        self.priority = priority
        self.message = message
        self.scheduled_at = scheduled_at
        self.release_at = release_at
        # None means the delivery never expires.
        self.expire_at = expire_at


class ActorRuntime:
    """Deterministic in-memory actor runtime."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._actors: dict[str, _Actor] = {}
        self._trace: list[TraceEntry] = []
        self._next_message_id = 1
        self._clock = 0
        # Pending timed deliveries, kept in scheduling (message-id) order;
        # _release_due scans and rebuilds it.
        self._scheduled: list[_ScheduledDelivery] = []

    # -- registration -----------------------------------------------------

    def register(self, name: str, initial_state: Any, handler: Handler) -> None:
        """Register a named actor.

        Raises :class:`ValueError` when ``name`` is empty or already
        registered; a failed registration changes nothing.
        """
        if not isinstance(name, str) or name == "":
            raise ValueError("actor name must be a non-empty string")
        if name in self._actors:
            raise ValueError(f"actor already registered: {name!r}")
        self._actors[name] = _Actor(
            name, copy.deepcopy(initial_state), handler, len(self._actors)
        )

    # -- delivery ---------------------------------------------------------

    def send(self, target: str, message: Any, priority: int = 0) -> int:
        """Deliver a message to ``target``'s mailbox and return its id.

        Ids are monotonically increasing within the runtime. Higher
        ``priority`` is processed first; equal priority is processed in id
        order. Raises :class:`TypeError` if ``priority`` is not an integer,
        :class:`LookupError` if ``target`` is unknown and
        :class:`ActorDataCopyError` if ``message`` cannot be deep-copied;
        a failed delivery consumes no id and changes no mailbox.
        """
        if not isinstance(priority, int) or isinstance(priority, bool):
            raise TypeError("priority must be an integer")
        actor = self._actors.get(target)
        if actor is None:
            raise LookupError(f"unknown actor: {target!r}")
        # Copy before assigning an id: a failed copy leaves the mailbox,
        # the trace, the actor state and the next message id untouched.
        stored = _copy_data("message", message)
        message_id = self._next_message_id
        self._next_message_id += 1
        heapq.heappush(actor.mailbox, (-priority, message_id, stored))
        return message_id

    def schedule(self, target: str, message: Any, delay: int,
                 ttl: int | None = None, priority: int = 0) -> int:
        """Schedule ``message`` for ``target`` at a future logical tick.

        Returns the delivery's id, taken from the same runtime-wide monotonic
        sequence as :meth:`send`. ``delay`` is the number of ticks counted
        from the current clock: the message is released when the clock reaches
        ``now + delay``. A ``delay`` of 0 releases it immediately unless it is
        already expired. ``ttl`` is the number of ticks the delivery stays
        alive after scheduling; when the clock reaches ``scheduled_at + ttl``
        the delivery expires without ever entering a mailbox or reaching a
        handler. At a tick that is both deadline and expiry, expiry wins.

        Raises :class:`TypeError` for wrong argument types, :class:`ValueError`
        for out-of-range ``delay``/``ttl``, :class:`LookupError` for an
        unknown ``target`` and :class:`ActorDataCopyError` if ``message``
        cannot be deep-copied; a failed schedule consumes no id and queues
        nothing.
        """
        if not isinstance(priority, int) or isinstance(priority, bool):
            raise TypeError("priority must be an integer")
        if not isinstance(delay, int) or isinstance(delay, bool):
            raise TypeError("delay must be an integer")
        if delay < 0:
            raise ValueError("delay must be a non-negative integer")
        if ttl is not None and (
            not isinstance(ttl, int) or isinstance(ttl, bool)
        ):
            raise TypeError("ttl must be None or an integer")
        if ttl is not None and ttl <= 0:
            raise ValueError("ttl must be a positive integer or None")
        actor = self._actors.get(target)
        if actor is None:
            raise LookupError(f"unknown actor: {target!r}")
        # Copy before assigning an id: a failed copy queues nothing and
        # consumes no id, exactly like send.
        stored = _copy_data("message", message)
        message_id = self._next_message_id
        self._next_message_id += 1
        scheduled_at = self._clock
        release_at = scheduled_at + delay
        expire_at = None if ttl is None else scheduled_at + ttl
        if delay == 0:
            # ttl is a strictly positive integer, so a zero-delay delivery is
            # never already expired: it enters the mailbox straight away.
            heapq.heappush(actor.mailbox, (-priority, message_id, stored))
        else:
            self._scheduled.append(
                _ScheduledDelivery(
                    message_id, actor, priority, stored,
                    scheduled_at, release_at, expire_at,
                )
            )
        return message_id

    # -- logical clock ----------------------------------------------------

    def clock(self) -> int:
        """Return the current logical tick (initially 0)."""
        return self._clock

    def advance(self, ticks: int) -> AdvanceResult:
        """Move the clock forward ``ticks`` and settle due deliveries.

        ``ticks`` must be a non-boolean positive integer; otherwise
        :class:`TypeError`/:class:`ValueError` is raised and nothing changes.
        The clock moves to the new tick first; then every pending delivery is
        settled: one whose deadline has been reached is released into its
        actor's mailbox with its scheduled id and priority, while one whose
        ttl has elapsed expires and is dropped. When both happen at the same
        tick expiry wins, so the message never reaches a handler. Released and
        expired ids are returned stably ordered by event tick and then by id.
        Releasing never invokes a handler and never writes a trace entry; use
        :meth:`run` afterwards to process the mail.
        """
        if not isinstance(ticks, int) or isinstance(ticks, bool):
            raise TypeError("ticks must be an integer")
        if ticks <= 0:
            raise ValueError("ticks must be a positive integer")

        new_time = self._clock + ticks
        released: list[tuple[int, int]] = []  # (release_at, id)
        expired: list[tuple[int, int]] = []   # (expire_at, id)
        remaining: list[_ScheduledDelivery] = []
        # _scheduled stays in message-id (scheduling) order; the event lists
        # are sorted by event tick and id afterwards, so the scan order is
        # irrelevant to the stable result.
        for delivery in self._scheduled:
            if (
                delivery.expire_at is not None
                and delivery.expire_at <= new_time
                and delivery.expire_at <= delivery.release_at
            ):
                # The ttl elapsed no later than the deadline: expiry at
                # expire_at. Equality with the deadline is decided in favour
                # of expiry, so a same-tick message never reaches a handler.
                expired.append((delivery.expire_at, delivery.message_id))
                continue
            if new_time >= delivery.release_at:
                # The deadline was reached during this advance. Even if the
                # ttl elapses at a later tick inside the same jump, the
                # delivery was released at its deadline and is ordinary
                # mailbox mail from then on; the ttl only guards the wait.
                heapq.heappush(
                    delivery.actor.mailbox,
                    (-delivery.priority, delivery.message_id,
                     delivery.message),
                )
                released.append((delivery.release_at, delivery.message_id))
                continue
            remaining.append(delivery)

        self._scheduled = remaining
        self._clock = new_time
        released.sort(key=lambda event: (event[0], event[1]))
        expired.sort(key=lambda event: (event[0], event[1]))
        return AdvanceResult(
            new_time,
            tuple(message_id for _, message_id in released),
            tuple(message_id for _, message_id in expired),
        )

    # -- execution --------------------------------------------------------
    def run(self, limit: int | None = None) -> int:
        """Process pending messages until mailboxes empty or ``limit`` hit.

        Derived messages become eligible only after the handling message
        completes. The first handler failure aborts the run: an ordinary
        exception is raised as :class:`ActorExecutionError`, while a
        :class:`BaseException` that is not an :class:`Exception` (such as
        :class:`KeyboardInterrupt`) propagates unchanged. A failure to
        deep-copy the state, the message, the handler result or a buffered
        derived message is raised as :class:`ActorExecutionError` whose
        ``original`` is an :class:`ActorDataCopyError`. Either way the
        failing message stays pending and nothing is committed for it.
        Returns the number of messages completed by this call.
        """
        if limit is not None and (
            not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool) or limit <= 0
        ):
            raise ValueError("limit must be a positive integer or None")

        processed = 0
        while limit is None or processed < limit:
            actor = None
            for candidate in self._actors.values():  # registration order
                if candidate.mailbox:
                    actor = candidate
                    break
            if actor is None:
                break

            neg_priority, message_id, message = heapq.heappop(actor.mailbox)
            priority = -neg_priority
            try:
                # Every copy the commit depends on is made up front, so a
                # copy failure (custom __deepcopy__, an exception raised
                # while copying) commits nothing: the message goes back to
                # the mailbox with its original priority and no state,
                # derived delivery, id or trace entry is produced.
                state_before = _copy_data(
                    "state before processing", actor.state
                )

                # Hand the handler private copies so a failure (including an
                # in-place mutation before raising) can never commit state
                # or alter the message kept in the mailbox.
                context = ActorContext(self)
                try:
                    new_state = actor.handler(
                        _copy_data("actor state", actor.state),
                        _copy_data("message", message),
                        context,
                    )
                except BaseException as exc:
                    # Ordinary exceptions are wrapped; BaseException
                    # subclasses that are not Exception (KeyboardInterrupt,
                    # SystemExit, ...) propagate unchanged.
                    if isinstance(exc, Exception):
                        raise ActorExecutionError(
                            actor.name, message_id, exc
                        ) from exc
                    raise

                # Stage the commit: the returned state and every buffered
                # derived message are copied before anything becomes
                # visible, so even a failure in the last derived copy hides
                # the earlier ones and consumes no id.
                committed_state = _copy_data("handler result", new_state)
                staged = [
                    (target, _copy_data("derived message", derived))
                    for target, derived in context._pending
                ]
                trace_state = _copy_data("handler result", committed_state)
            except ActorDataCopyError as exc:
                heapq.heappush(actor.mailbox, (neg_priority, message_id, message))
                raise ActorExecutionError(
                    actor.name, message_id, exc
                ) from exc
            except BaseException:
                # Keep the message unacknowledged; commit nothing. The
                # message stays pending either way.
                heapq.heappush(actor.mailbox, (neg_priority, message_id, message))
                raise

            # Commit: only runtime-owned bookkeeping below, so nothing here
            # can fail because of user data. Derived sends enqueue only
            # after successful completion.
            for derived_target, stored in staged:
                derived_id = self._next_message_id
                self._next_message_id += 1
                derived_actor = self._actors[derived_target]
                heapq.heappush(derived_actor.mailbox, (0, derived_id, stored))

            actor.state = committed_state
            self._trace.append(
                TraceEntry(
                    message_id=message_id,
                    actor_name=actor.name,
                    priority=priority,
                    state_before=state_before,
                    state_after=trace_state,
                )
            )
            processed += 1

        return processed

    # -- read-only queries ------------------------------------------------

    def get_state(self, actor_name: str) -> Any:
        """Return an independent snapshot of the actor's current state."""
        actor = self._require_actor(actor_name)
        return copy.deepcopy(actor.state)

    def pending_count(self, actor_name: str) -> int:
        """Return the number of unprocessed messages for the actor.

        Only messages that have already entered the mailbox are counted;
        scheduled deliveries that have not been released (and not expired) are
        reported separately by :meth:`scheduled_count`.
        """
        actor = self._require_actor(actor_name)
        return len(actor.mailbox)

    def scheduled_count(self, actor_name: str) -> int:
        """Return the actor's deliveries neither released nor expired.

        Raises :class:`LookupError` for an unknown actor.
        """
        actor = self._require_actor(actor_name)
        return sum(
            1 for delivery in self._scheduled if delivery.actor is actor
        )

    def trace(self) -> list[TraceEntry]:
        """Return completed processings in completion order.

        A fresh list of independent snapshots is returned each time; mutating
        it or the states inside entries cannot affect the runtime.
        """
        return copy.deepcopy(self._trace)

    def _require_actor(self, name: str) -> _Actor:
        actor = self._actors.get(name)
        if actor is None:
            raise LookupError(f"unknown actor: {name!r}")
        return actor

22	from actor_runtime import ActorRuntime, ActorContext
23	
24	def counter(state, message, ctx: ActorContext):
25	    state = dict(state)
26	    state[message] = state.get(message, 0) + 1
27	    if state[message] == 1:
28	        ctx.send("logger", f"first sighting of {message}")
29	    return state
30	
31	rt = ActorRuntime()
32	rt.register("counter", {}, counter)
33	rt.register("logger", [], lambda s, m, ctx: s + [m])
34	
35	msg_id = rt.send("counter", "hello", priority=10)  # -> 1, monotonic
36	rt.send("counter", "hello")                        # default priority 0
37	rt.run()                  # process until all mailboxes are empty
38	rt.run(limit=5)           # or process at most 5 messages
39	
40	rt.get_state("counter")   # independent snapshot of current state
41	rt.pending_count("counter")
42	rt.trace()                # list of TraceEntry, in completion order
43	```
44	
45	### Logical clock and timed delivery
46	
47	Time is an explicitly replayed input, never wall-clock time: a logical clock
48	starts at 0 and only moves when `advance` is called.
49	
50	```python
51	rt.clock()                          # -> 0, the current logical tick
52	mid = rt.schedule("counter", "later", delay=5, ttl=10, priority=0)
53	# mid comes from the same runtime-wide monotonic sequence as send.
54	# delay: ticks from the current tick until the message is released.
55	# ttl:   optional ticks (measured from scheduling) the delivery stays alive;
56	#        None (the default) means it never expires.
57	
58	result = rt.advance(5)              # AdvanceResult(time=5, released=(mid,), expired=())
59	# result.released / result.expired are immutable tuples of message ids,
60	# stably ordered by the tick the event happened at and then by message id.
61	rt.pending_count("counter")         # released mail is ordinary mailbox mail
62	rt.scheduled_count("counter")       # deliveries neither released nor expired
63	rt.run()                            # advance never invokes a handler
64	```
65	
66	- `delay=0` releases immediately into the mailbox; `schedule` itself never
67	  moves the clock, and neither does `run`.
68	- A delivery is released when `now >= scheduled_at + delay`; it expires when
69	  `now >= scheduled_at + ttl`. When both happen on the same tick, expiry is
70	  decided first, so the message never enters a mailbox or reaches a handler.
71	  A delivery already released is ordinary mail — a later ttl tick does not
72	  remove it.
73	- Released messages keep the id returned by `schedule` and their scheduled
74	  priority, so they participate in the usual registration-order /
75	  priority / id scheduling. They only enter the trace after a successful
76	  `run`, exactly like `send` messages; expired messages produce no handler
77	  call, no trace entry and no state change.
78	- Validation: `priority` must be a non-boolean integer (`TypeError`
79	  otherwise); `delay` must be a non-boolean non-negative integer
80	  (`TypeError`/`ValueError`); `ttl` must be `None` or a non-boolean positive
81	  integer; `advance` takes a non-boolean positive integer. Unknown targets
82	  raise `LookupError`; an uncopyable scheduled message raises
83	  `ActorDataCopyError` and consumes no id. Any failed `schedule`/`advance`
84	  leaves the clock, the id counter and every queue untouched.
85	
86	### Semantics
87	
88	- An actor is a unique non-empty string name, an initial state and a handler
89	  `handler(state, message, ctx) -> new_state`. Registering an empty or
90	  duplicate name raises `ValueError`.
91	- `send(target, message, priority=0)` returns a runtime-wide monotonic
92	  message id and enqueues a private copy in the actor's mailbox. Unknown
93	  targets raise `LookupError`; non-integer priority raises `TypeError`; a
94	  message that cannot be deep-copied raises `ActorDataCopyError`.
95	  Failed deliveries consume no id.
96	- Scheduling: the actor with the earliest registration order and a non-empty
97	  mailbox is selected; within a mailbox, higher priority wins, then lower
98	  message id. Messages a handler sends through `ctx.send` are enqueued only
99	  after the handler returns successfully.
100	- Atomic commit: state and derived deliveries are committed together only
101	  after the handler returns normally and every result has been copied. If
102	  the handler raises, or copying the state, the message, the handler result
103	  or a buffered derived message fails, the message stays unacknowledged,
104	  nothing is committed (no state, no derived delivery, no id, no trace
105	  entry) and `run` raises `ActorExecutionError` (exposing `actor_name`,
106	  `message_id` and `original` — an `ActorDataCopyError` for copy
107	  failures); earlier completed messages remain committed.
108	- `run(limit=None)` processes until idle; a non-positive or non-integer
109	  `limit` raises `ValueError` without consuming any message. `BaseException`
110	  subclasses (e.g. `KeyboardInterrupt`) propagate unwrapped.
111	- `get_state`, `pending_count` and `trace` are read-only and return
112	  independent copies; unknown actors raise `LookupError`. Each
113	  `TraceEntry` has `message_id`, `actor_name`, `priority`, `state_before`
114	  and `state_after`.
115	
116	Only single-process in-memory semantics are provided: no persistence,
117	supervision or parallel scheduling. Time is logical and only advances via
118	explicit `advance` calls — there is no wall-clock access and no threads.
119	
120	## Tests
121	
122	```bash
123	python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
124	```

# actor-runtime

Deterministic actor runtime.

Pure-Python, no runtime dependencies. Requires Python 3.10+.

## Usage

```bash
python3 -m actor_runtime version
python3 -m actor_runtime help
```

## In-memory actor runtime

Register named actors, deliver messages to their mailboxes and explicitly
advance the runtime. Processing order is fully deterministic and depends only
on registration order, message priority and delivery id — never on wall-clock
time, randomness or threads.

```python
from actor_runtime import ActorRuntime, ActorContext

def counter(state, message, ctx: ActorContext):
    state = dict(state)
    state[message] = state.get(message, 0) + 1
    if state[message] == 1:
        ctx.send("logger", f"first sighting of {message}")
    return state

rt = ActorRuntime()
rt.register("counter", {}, counter)
rt.register("logger", [], lambda s, m, ctx: s + [m])

msg_id = rt.send("counter", "hello", priority=10)  # -> 1, monotonic
rt.send("counter", "hello")                        # default priority 0
rt.run()                  # process until all mailboxes are empty
rt.run(limit=5)           # or process at most 5 messages

rt.get_state("counter")   # independent snapshot of current state
rt.pending_count("counter")
rt.trace()                # list of TraceEntry, in completion order
```

### Logical clock and timed delivery

Time is an explicitly replayed input, never wall-clock time: a logical clock
starts at 0 and only moves when `advance` is called.

```python
rt.clock()                          # -> 0, the current logical tick
mid = rt.schedule("counter", "later", delay=5, ttl=10, priority=0)
# mid comes from the same runtime-wide monotonic sequence as send.
# delay: ticks from the current tick until the message is released.
# ttl:   optional ticks (measured from scheduling) the delivery stays alive;
#        None (the default) means it never expires.

result = rt.advance(5)              # AdvanceResult(time=5, released=(mid,), expired=())
# result.released / result.expired are immutable tuples of message ids,
# stably ordered by the tick the event happened at and then by message id.
rt.pending_count("counter")         # released mail is ordinary mailbox mail
rt.scheduled_count("counter")       # deliveries neither released nor expired
rt.run()                            # advance never invokes a handler
```

- `delay=0` releases immediately into the mailbox; `schedule` itself never
  moves the clock, and neither does `run`.
- A delivery is released when `now >= scheduled_at + delay`; it expires when
  `now >= scheduled_at + ttl`. When both happen on the same tick, expiry is
  decided first, so the message never enters a mailbox or reaches a handler.
  A delivery already released is ordinary mail — a later ttl tick does not
  remove it.
- Released messages keep the id returned by `schedule` and their scheduled
  priority, so they participate in the usual registration-order /
  priority / id scheduling. They only enter the trace after a successful
  `run`, exactly like `send` messages; expired messages produce no handler
  call, no trace entry and no state change.
- Validation: `priority` must be a non-boolean integer (`TypeError`
  otherwise); `delay` must be a non-boolean non-negative integer
  (`TypeError`/`ValueError`); `ttl` must be `None` or a non-boolean positive
  integer; `advance` takes a non-boolean positive integer. Unknown targets
  raise `LookupError`; an uncopyable scheduled message raises
  `ActorDataCopyError` and consumes no id. Any failed `schedule`/`advance`
  leaves the clock, the id counter and every queue untouched.

### Semantics

- An actor is a unique non-empty string name, an initial state and a handler
  `handler(state, message, ctx) -> new_state`. Registering an empty or
  duplicate name raises `ValueError`.
- `send(target, message, priority=0)` returns a runtime-wide monotonic
  message id and enqueues a private copy in the actor's mailbox. Unknown
  targets raise `LookupError`; non-integer priority raises `TypeError`; a
  message that cannot be deep-copied raises `ActorDataCopyError`.
  Failed deliveries consume no id.
- Scheduling: the actor with the earliest registration order and a non-empty
  mailbox is selected; within a mailbox, higher priority wins, then lower
  message id. Messages a handler sends through `ctx.send` are enqueued only
  after the handler returns successfully.
- Atomic commit: state and derived deliveries are committed together only
  after the handler returns normally and every result has been copied. If
  the handler raises, or copying the state, the message, the handler result
  or a buffered derived message fails, the message stays unacknowledged,
  nothing is committed (no state, no derived delivery, no id, no trace
  entry) and `run` raises `ActorExecutionError` (exposing `actor_name`,
  `message_id` and `original` — an `ActorDataCopyError` for copy
  failures); earlier completed messages remain committed.
- `run(limit=None)` processes until idle; a non-positive or non-integer
  `limit` raises `ValueError` without consuming any message. `BaseException`
  subclasses (e.g. `KeyboardInterrupt`) propagate unwrapped.
- `get_state`, `pending_count` and `trace` are read-only and return
  independent copies; unknown actors raise `LookupError`. Each
  `TraceEntry` has `message_id`, `actor_name`, `priority`, `state_before`
  and `state_after`.

Only single-process in-memory semantics are provided: no persistence,
supervision or parallel scheduling. Time is logical and only advances via
explicit `advance` calls — there is no wall-clock access and no threads.

83	class DeterministicRng:
84	    """xorshift64*: a tiny fixed PRNG with stable cross-run behaviour.

87	    semantics are a CPython implementation detail replay equivalence should

91	    MULT = 0x2545F4914F6CDD1D
92	    MASK = (1 << 64) - 1

94	    def __init__(self, seed: int):
95	        state = int(seed) & self.MASK
96	        if state == 0:
97	            state = 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15  # xorshift never allows a zero state
98	        self._state = state

100	    def next_u64(self) -> int:
101	        x = self._state
102	        x ^= (x >> 12) & self.MASK
103	        x ^= (x << 25) & self.MASK
104	        x ^= (x >> 27) & self.MASK
105	        x &= self.MASK
106	        self._state = x
107	        return (x * self.MULT) & self.MASK
108	
109	    def below(self, n: int) -> int:
110	        if n <= 0:
111	            raise ValueError("n must be positive")
112	        return self.next_u64() % n

114	    def choose(self, seq):
115	        return seq[self.below(len(seq))]

118	        """Return True with probability ``pct`` percent."""
119	        return self.below(100) < pct

121	    def randint(self, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
122	        return lo + self.below(hi - lo + 1)

148	def _dedup_then(state, message, mut, after):
149	    """Apply ``mut`` once per dedup id; ``after`` runs only on first apply.

157	        return {

159	            "arrivals": state["arrivals"] + [
160	                {"kind": message["kind"], "duplicate": True}
161	            ],
162	            "value": state["value"],
163	        }
164	    new_state = {

326	def _read_frame(stream: io.BytesIO, *, require_header: bool) -> Optional[dict]:
327	    header = stream.read(4)
328	    if not header:
329	        return None
330	    if len(header) != 4:
331	        raise CorruptRecordError("truncated record header")
332	    (length,) = struct.unpack("<I", header)
333	    body = stream.read(length)
334	    if len(body) != length:
335	        raise CorruptRecordError("truncated record body")
336	    try:
337	        rec = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))
338	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
339	        raise CorruptRecordError(f"undecodable record: {exc}") from exc
340	    if not isinstance(rec, dict) or "t" not in rec:
341	        raise CorruptRecordError("record missing type tag")
342	    if require_header and rec.get("t") != "header":
343	        raise CorruptRecordError("journal missing header frame")
344	    if rec.get("t") == "header":
345	        if rec.get("schema") != SCHEMA_VERSION:
346	            raise IncompatibleSnapshotError(
347	                f"journal schema {rec.get('schema')!r} incompatible "
348	                f"with {SCHEMA_VERSION}"
349	            )
350	        if rec.get("codec") != CODEC:

495	    last_resolve = max(resolve_positions, default=-1)

536	            original = originals[cmd[1]]
537	            records.append({
538	                "t": "deliver",
539	                "target": original["target"],
540	                "message": dict(original["message"]),
541	                "priority": original["priority"],
542	                "dedup": original["dedup"],
543	                "redelivery": True,
544	            })
545	        elif op == SCHEDULE:
546	            _, target, token, delay, ttl, priority, want_dedup = cmd
547	            t_seq += 1
548	            timer_id = f"t{t_seq:04d}"
549	            records.append({
550	                "t": "schedule",
551	                "id": timer_id,
552	                "target": target,
553	                "token": token,
554	                "delay": int(delay),
555	                "ttl": int(ttl),
556	                "priority": int(priority),
557	                "dedup": timer_id if want_dedup else None,
558	            })
559	        elif op == CLOCK:
560	            records.append({"t": "clock", "ticks": int(cmd[1])})
561	        elif op == CAP:
562	            n = cmd[1]
563	            records.append({"t": "cap", "n": None if n is None else int(n)})
564	        elif op == RESOLVE:
565	            records.append({"t": "resolve"})
566	        elif op == SNAPSHOT:
567	            snap_seq += 1
568	            records.append({"t": "snapshot", "seq": snap_seq})
569	        else:
570	            raise InvalidScript(f"unknown command: {op!r}")
571	    return records

611	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
612	# Supervision policy
613	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
614	#
615	# Deterministic from public failure facts only:
616	#   child      : first fault -> restart, further faults -> escalate
617	#   counter    : always resume
618	#   events     : always stop
619	#   supervisor : always escalate
620	
621	DEFAULT_POLICY_OUTCOMES = {
622	    A_CHILD: ("restart", "escalate"),
623	    A_COUNTER: ("resume", "resume"),
624	    A_EVENTS: ("stop", "stop"),
625	    A_SUPERVISOR: ("escalate", "escalate"),
626	}
627	
628	
629	def default_policy(actor_name: str, attempts: int) -> str:
630	    outcomes = DEFAULT_POLICY_OUTCOMES[actor_name]
631	    return outcomes[min(attempts - 1, len(outcomes) - 1)]

638	
639	class Interpreter:
640	    def __init__(self, *, policy: Callable[[str, int], str] = default_policy):
641	        self.policy = policy
642	        self.rt = ActorRuntime()
643	        register_all(self.rt)
644	        self.clock = 0
645	        self.cap: Optional[int] = None
646	        self.stopped: set[str] = set()
647	        self.attempts: dict[str, int] = {}
648	        self.timers: list[PendingTimer] = []
649	        self.events: list[dict] = []
650	        self.supervision: list[dict] = []
651	        self.delivered_dedup: list[dict] = []
652	        self.pending_fault: Optional[dict] = None
653	        self.snapshots: list[tuple] = []
654	
655	    # -- snapshots --------------------------------------------------------
656	
657	    def snapshot_blob(self) -> bytes:
658	        states = {}
659	        for name in ACTOR_NAMES:
660	            states[name] = {"stopped": True} if name in self.stopped \
661	                else canonical_state(self.rt.get_state(name))
662	        payload = {
663	            "snapshot": {
664	                "schema": SCHEMA_VERSION,
665	                "codec": CODEC,
666	                "cap": self.cap,
667	                "clock": self.clock,
668	                "stopped": sorted(self.stopped),
669	                "attempts": dict(self.attempts),
670	                "states": states,
671	                "timers": [
672	                    {
673	                        "fire_at": t.fire_at,
674	                        "expire_at": t.expire_at,
675	                        "target": t.target,
676	                        "message": t.message,
677	                        "priority": t.priority,
678	                        "id": t.timer_id,
679	                    }
680	                    for t in self.timers
681	                ],
682	                "trace": [
683	                    [
684	                        e.message_id, e.actor_name, e.priority,
685	                        canonical_state(e.state_before),
686	                        canonical_state(e.state_after),
687	                    ]
688	                    for e in self.rt.trace()
689	                ],
690	                "events": list(self.events),
691	                "supervision": list(self.supervision),
692	                "delivered_dedup": list(self.delivered_dedup),
693	            }
694	        }
695	        return _json_dumps(payload)
696	
697	    def load_snapshot(self, blob: bytes) -> int:
698	        try:
699	            outer = _json_loads(blob)
700	        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
701	            raise CorruptRecordError(f"undecodable snapshot: {exc}") from exc
702	        snap = outer.get("snapshot") if isinstance(outer, dict) else None
703	        if not isinstance(snap, dict):
704	            raise CorruptRecordError("snapshot missing payload")
705	        if snap.get("schema") != SCHEMA_VERSION:
706	            raise IncompatibleSnapshotError(
707	                f"snapshot schema {snap.get('schema')!r} incompatible "
708	                f"with {SCHEMA_VERSION}"
709	            )
710	        if snap.get("codec") != CODEC:
711	            raise IncompatibleSnapshotError(
712	                f"snapshot codec {snap.get('codec')!r} unsupported"
713	            )
714	        self.cap = snap["cap"]
715	        self.clock = int(snap["clock"])
716	        self.stopped = set(snap.get("stopped", []))
717	        self.attempts = dict(snap.get("attempts", {}))
718	        self.timers = [
719	            PendingTimer(
720	                fire_at=int(t["fire_at"]),
721	                expire_at=int(t["expire_at"]),
722	                target=t["target"],
723	                message=t["message"],
724	                priority=int(t["priority"]),
725	                timer_id=t["id"],
726	            )
727	            for t in snap.get("timers", [])
728	        ]
729	        self.events = list(snap["events"])
730	        self.supervision = list(snap["supervision"])
731	        self.delivered_dedup = list(snap["delivered_dedup"])
732	        # Restore through the public registration entry point: the snapshot
733	        # state becomes the new runtime generation's initial state.
734	        self.rt = ActorRuntime()
735	        for name in ACTOR_NAMES:
736	            raw = snap["states"][name]
737	            if isinstance(raw, dict) and raw.get("stopped"):
738	                state = initial_state_for(name)
739	            elif name == A_SUPERVISOR:
740	                state = {
741	                    "observed": list(raw["observed"]),
742	                    "escalations": list(raw["escalations"]),
743	                }
744	            else:
745	                state = {
746	                    "seen": set(raw["seen"]),
747	                    "arrivals": list(raw["arrivals"]),
748	                    "value": raw["value"],
749	                }
750	            self.rt.register(name, state, HANDLERS[name])
751	        self._stored_trace = [tuple(e) for e in snap["trace"]]
752	        return len(self._stored_trace)
753	
754	    # -- record processing ------------------------------------------------
755	
756	    @staticmethod
757	    def _faulting_positions(records: list[dict]) -> set[int]:
758	        """Deliver positions immediately followed by their fault resolution.
759	
760	        Adjacency is guaranteed by validate_script: the faulting delivery is
761	        the last durable input before the resolve (first run) or supervision
762	        (replay) record the failure produced.
763	        """
764	        out = set()
765	        for i in range(len(records) - 1):
766	            rec, nxt = records[i], records[i + 1]
767	            if (rec.get("t") == "deliver"
768	                    and nxt.get("t") in ("resolve", "supervision")
769	                    and (nxt.get("t") == "resolve"
770	                         or nxt.get("actor") == rec.get("target"))):
771	                out.add(i)
772	        return out
773	
774	    @staticmethod
775	    def _restart_positions(records: list[dict]) -> dict[str, int]:
776	        return {
777	            rec["actor"]: i
778	            for i, rec in enumerate(records)
779	            if rec.get("t") == "supervision" and rec.get("action") == "restart"
780	        }
781	
782	    def run_records(self, records: list[dict], *, rebuild: bool = False):
783	        # Faulting positions are structural (fail adjoins resolve), so they
784	        # are known on the first run too; restart positions only exist once
785	        # resolves have been concretised, i.e. during rebuild.
786	        faulting = self._faulting_positions(records)
787	        restart_positions = (
788	            self._restart_positions(records) if rebuild else {}
789	        )
790	        for i, rec in enumerate(records):
791	            self._step(rec, i, rebuild, faulting, restart_positions)
792	        return self._result()
793	
794	    def _step(self, rec, i, rebuild, faulting, restart_positions) -> None:
795	        kind = rec["t"]
796	        if kind == "cap":
797	            self.cap = rec["n"]
798	            self.events.append({"at": "cap", "n": rec["n"]})
799	            # Restoring the cap to None drains to quiescence; tightening the
800	            # cap only affects future external inputs (nothing to re-drain).
801	            if rec["n"] is None:
802	                self._drain()
803	        elif kind == "deliver":
804	            self._step_deliver(rec, i, rebuild, faulting, restart_positions)
805	            self._drain()
806	        elif kind == "schedule":
807	            self._step_schedule(rec)
808	        elif kind == "clock":
809	            self._step_clock(rec, i, rebuild, restart_positions)
810	            self._drain()
811	        elif kind == "resolve":
812	            raise InvalidScript("resolve must be concretised before replay")
813	        elif kind == "supervision":
814	            self._step_supervision(rec)
815	            self._drain()
816	        elif kind == "snapshot":
817	            # Marker event is logged *before* the blob is captured, so a
818	            # recovery that skips this frame still observes the marker.
819	            self.events.append({"at": "snapshot", "seq": rec["seq"]})
820	            self.snapshots.append((rec["seq"], self.snapshot_blob()))
821	        else:
822	            raise CorruptRecordError(f"unknown record type: {kind!r}")
823	
824	    def _step_deliver(self, rec, i, rebuild, faulting,
825	                      restart_positions) -> None:
826	        target = rec["target"]
827	        message = dict(rec["message"])
828	        if rec.get("dedup") is not None:
829	            message["dedup"] = rec["dedup"]
830	        is_faulting = rebuild and i in faulting
831	        erased_by_restart = (
832	            rebuild and not is_faulting
833	            and target in RESTARTABLE
834	            and i < restart_positions.get(target, -1)
835	        )
836	        discarded = is_faulting or erased_by_restart
837	        # The delivery did enter a live actor mailbox unless the actor was
838	        # already stopped; a faulting/restart-erased delivery is separately
839	        # marked discarded by supervision rather than refused up front.
840	        accepted = target not in self.stopped
841	        if accepted and not discarded:
842	            self.rt.send(target, message, priority=int(rec["priority"]))
843	        self.events.append({
844	            "at": "deliver",
845	            "target": target,
846	            "kind": message["kind"],
847	            "priority": int(rec["priority"]),
848	            "dedup": rec.get("dedup"),
849	            "redelivery": bool(rec.get("redelivery")),
850	            "accepted": accepted,
851	            "discarded": discarded,
852	        })
853	        if rec.get("dedup") is not None:
854	            self.delivered_dedup.append({
855	                "dedup": rec["dedup"],
856	                "duplicate": bool(rec.get("redelivery")),
857	            })
858	
859	    def _step_schedule(self, rec) -> None:
860	        message = {"kind": "timer", "token": rec["token"]}
861	        if rec.get("dedup") is not None:
862	            message["dedup"] = rec["dedup"]
863	        fire_at = self.clock + int(rec["delay"])
864	        self.timers.append(PendingTimer(
865	            fire_at=fire_at,
866	            expire_at=fire_at + int(rec["ttl"]),
867	            target=rec["target"],
868	            message=message,
869	            priority=int(rec["priority"]),
870	            timer_id=rec["id"],
871	        ))
872	        self.events.append({
873	            "at": "schedule",
874	            "id": rec["id"],
875	            "target": rec["target"],
876	            "fire_at": fire_at,
877	        })
878	
879	    def _step_clock(self, rec, i, rebuild, restart_positions) -> None:
880	        self.clock += int(rec["ticks"])
881	        self.events.append({
882	            "at": "clock",
883	            "ticks": int(rec["ticks"]),
884	            "new_clock": self.clock,
885	        })
886	        due = [t for t in self.timers if t.fire_at <= self.clock]
887	        due.sort(key=lambda t: (t.fire_at, t.timer_id))
888	        self.timers = [t for t in self.timers if t.fire_at > self.clock]
889	        for timer in due:
890	            if self.clock >= timer.expire_at:
891	                # Expired at/before it became eligible: never enqueued, never
892	                # reaches a handler. ttl == 0 expires at the deadline itself.
893	                self.events.append({
894	                    "at": "timer_expired",
895	                    "id": timer.timer_id,
896	                    "target": timer.target,
897	                })
898	                continue
899	            erased_by_restart = (
900	                rebuild and timer.target in RESTARTABLE
901	                and i < restart_positions.get(timer.target, -1)
902	            )
903	            delivered = (
904	                timer.target not in self.stopped and not erased_by_restart
905	            )
906	            if delivered:
907	                self.rt.send(
908	                    timer.target, timer.message, priority=timer.priority
909	                )
910	            self.events.append({
911	                "at": "timer_fired",
912	                "id": timer.timer_id,
913	                "target": timer.target,
914	                "delivered": delivered,
915	            })
916	            self.delivered_dedup.append({
917	                "dedup": timer.timer_id,
918	                "duplicate": False,
919	            })
920	
921	    def _step_supervision(self, rec) -> None:
922	        actor = rec["actor"]
923	        action = rec["action"]
924	        self.attempts[actor] = self.attempts.get(actor, 0) + 1
925	        self.events.append({
926	            "at": "fault",
927	            "actor": actor,
928	            "message_id": rec["message_id"],
929	            "error_type": rec["error_type"],
930	        })
931	        self.events.append({
932	            "at": "supervision",
933	            "actor": actor,
934	            "message_id": rec["message_id"],
935	            "action": action,
936	        })
937	        self.supervision.append({
938	            "actor": actor,
939	            "message_id": rec["message_id"],
940	            "error_type": rec["error_type"],
941	            "action": action,
942	        })
943	        if action in ("stop", "escalate"):
944	            self.stopped.add(actor)
945	        if action == "escalate" and actor == A_CHILD:
946	            self.rt.send(A_SUPERVISOR, {"kind": "escalated", "key": actor})
947	
948	    def supervision_record_for_pending(self) -> dict:
949	        assert self.pending_fault is not None
950	        fault = self.pending_fault
951	        actor = fault["actor"]
952	        attempts = self.attempts.get(actor, 0) + 1
953	        return {
954	            "t": "supervision",
955	            "actor": actor,
956	            "message_id": fault["message_id"],
957	            "error_type": fault["error_type"],
958	            "action": self.policy(actor, attempts),
959	        }
960	
961	    # -- scheduling -------------------------------------------------------
962	
963	    def _live_actors_with_mail(self) -> bool:
964	        return any(
965	            name not in self.stopped and self.rt.pending_count(name) > 0
966	            for name in ACTOR_NAMES
967	        )
968	
969	    def _drain(self) -> None:
970	        """Process pending messages under the configured cap.
971	
972	        No cap: run to idle (the runtime's documented registration / priority
973	        / id order).  Cap N: at most N completions per external input; each
974	        step is one public ``run(limit=1)``.  No wall-clock waits, no threads.
975	        """
976	        if self.pending_fault is not None:
977	            return
978	        budget = self.cap
979	        while self._live_actors_with_mail():
980	            try:
981	                if budget is None:
982	                    self.rt.run()
983	                    return
984	                self.rt.run(limit=1)
985	            except ActorExecutionError as exc:
986	                self.pending_fault = {
987	                    "actor": exc.actor_name,
988	                    "message_id": exc.message_id,
989	                    "error_type": type(exc.original).__name__,
990	                }
991	                return
992	            budget -= 1
993	            if budget == 0:
994	                return
995	
996	    # -- result -----------------------------------------------------------
997	
998	    def _states(self) -> dict:
999	        return {
1000	            name: ({"stopped": True} if name in self.stopped
1001	                   else canonical_state(self.rt.get_state(name)))
1002	            for name in ACTOR_NAMES
1003	        }
1004	
1005	    def _live_trace(self) -> list:
1006	        return [
1007	            (
1008	                e.message_id, e.actor_name, e.priority,
1009	                canonical_state(e.state_before),
1010	                canonical_state(e.state_after),
1011	            )
1012	            for e in self.rt.trace()
1013	        ]
1014	
1015	    def _result(self, stored_trace: Optional[list] = None) -> ScenarioResult:
1016	        live = self._live_trace()
1017	        traces = (list(stored_trace) + live) if stored_trace else live
1018	        return ScenarioResult(
1019	            states=self._states(),
1020	            traces=traces,
1021	            events=list(self.events),
1022	            supervision=list(self.supervision),
1023	            delivered_dedup=list(self.delivered_dedup),
1024	            restored_len=len(stored_trace) if stored_trace else 0,
1025	            snapshots=list(self.snapshots),
1026	        )

1029	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1030	# Facade: first run / journal replay / snapshot recovery
1031	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1032	
1033	
1034	def _process(records, *, rebuild_trigger: str, policy):
1035	    """Shared driver: feed records one at a time, rebuilding at boundaries.
1036	
1037	    ``rebuild_trigger`` is ``"resolve"`` (first run; record is concretised
1038	    using the live fault) or ``"supervision"`` (replay; record already
1039	    concrete).
1040	    """
1041	    interp = Interpreter(policy=policy)
1042	    i = 0
1043	    while i < len(records):
1044	        rec = records[i]
1045	        if rec.get("t") != rebuild_trigger:
1046	            interp.run_records([rec])
1047	            i += 1
1048	            continue
1049	        if rebuild_trigger == "resolve":
1050	            if interp.pending_fault is None:
1051	                raise InvalidScript("resolve without a pending fault")
1052	            records[i] = interp.supervision_record_for_pending()
1053	        # Rebuild the whole durable prefix through a fresh public runtime,
1054	        # honouring every supervision decision so far.
1055	        rebuilt = Interpreter(policy=policy)
1056	        rebuilt.run_records(records[: i + 1], rebuild=True)
1057	        assert rebuilt.pending_fault is None
1058	        interp = rebuilt
1059	        i += 1
1060	    return interp
1061	
1062	
1063	def execute(script: list, *,
1064	            policy: Callable[[str, int], str] = default_policy
1065	            ) -> ScenarioResult:
1066	    """First execution: normalise, interpret, and return journal + result."""
1067	    records = normalize_script(script)
1068	    interp = _process(records, rebuild_trigger=RESOLVE, policy=policy)
1069	    journal = encode_records(records)
1070	    result = interp._result()
1071	    result.journal = journal
1072	
1073	    # Replace the interpreter's (seq, blob) pairs with (seq, offset, blob),
1074	    # the offset being the snapshot marker frame's position in the journal.
1075	    offsets = frame_offsets(journal)  # [0] = header; record k at index k+1
1076	    located = []
1077	    for seq, blob in interp.snapshots:
1078	        for k, rec in enumerate(records):
1079	            if rec.get("t") == "snapshot" and rec["seq"] == seq:
1080	                located.append((seq, offsets[k + 1], blob))
1081	                break
1082	    result.snapshots = located
1083	    return result
1084	
1085	
1086	def replay_journal(journal: bytes, *,
1087	                   policy: Callable[[str, int], str] = default_policy
1088	                   ) -> ScenarioResult:
1089	    """Reconstruct a result from durable bytes alone."""
1090	    records = parse_records(journal)
1091	    interp = _process(records, rebuild_trigger="supervision", policy=policy)
1092	    result = interp._result()
1093	    result.journal = journal
1094	    return result

1097	def recover_snapshot(snapshot_blob: bytes, journal: bytes, *,
1098	                     marker_offset: int,
1099	                     policy: Callable[[str, int], str] = default_policy
1100	                     ) -> ScenarioResult:
1101	    """Restore from the snapshot, then apply the journal suffix."""
1102	    interp = Interpreter(policy=policy)
1103	    restored_len = interp.load_snapshot(snapshot_blob)
1104	    stored_trace = list(interp._stored_trace)
1105	
1106	    offsets = frame_offsets(journal)
1107	    end_offsets = offsets[1:] + [len(journal)]
1108	    suffix_start = None
1109	    for off, end in zip(offsets, end_offsets):
1110	        if off == marker_offset:
1111	            suffix_start = end
1112	            break
1113	    if suffix_start is None:
1114	        raise CorruptRecordError("snapshot marker not found in journal")
1115	    suffix = (
1116	        parse_records(
1117	            journal, start_offset=suffix_start, require_header=False
1118	        )
1119	        if suffix_start < len(journal) else []
1120	    )
1121	    for rec in suffix:
1122	        if rec.get("t") in ("supervision", "resolve"):
1123	            # Script invariant: supervision always precedes snapshots.
1124	            raise InvalidScript(
1125	                "recovery suffix must not contain supervision records"
1126	            )
1127	        interp.run_records([rec])
1128	    result = interp._result(stored_trace=stored_trace)
1129	    result.journal = journal
